title: solvecdp
text: solvecdp is fastcdp for solveit: the same async Python client for the Chrome DevTools Protocol, but driving the user’s own browser from a solveit kernel. Every CDP domain is a Python attribute with auto-generated signatures and docstrings, plus event subscription, navigation and form helpers, accessibility tree access, and console/network/dialog debugging buffers. Since the kernel runs on a remote server, frames are relayed through rustygate’s /api/wsx websocket channel (exposed to browsers at /rusty/api/wsx) to the solveit-chrome extension, which executes them with chrome.debugger.

title: solvecdp
text:
Installation
You must install the solveit-chrome extension before using solvecdp.
Solveit already has solvecdp installed, but if you want to install the latest you can get it from pypi:
$ pip install solvecdp

title: solvecdp
text:
How to use

from solvecdp import *


The JsCDP class
Every CDP domain is available as an attribute with auto-generated signatures. You can search for commands with cdp_search:

cdp_search('screenshot')

"Emulation.setVisibleSize: Resizes the frame/viewport of the page. Note that this does not affect the frame's container\n(e.g. browser window). Can \nHeadlessExperimental.beginFrame: Sends a BeginFrame to the target and returns when the frame was completed. Optionally captures a\nscreenshot from the res\n  evt Overlay.screenshotRequested: Fired when user asks to capture screenshot of some area on the page.\nPage.captureScreenshot: Capture page screenshot."


Connect (one connection per browser), then open a tab:

cdp = await JsCDP.connect()
page = await cdp.new_page()

Go to a page:

await page.goto('https://httpbingo.org/forms/post')

Eval js:

await page.eval('document.title')

'6. httpbin.org/forms/post'


Or you can wait_for any js expression to be truthy, and have it returned:

await page.wait_for('document.title')

'6. httpbin.org/forms/post'


Take a screenshot of the page:

img = await page.screenshot()

Clean up when done:

await page.close()

See JsCDP docs for full details.

title: solvecdp
text:
Filling forms

page = await cdp.new_page(url='https://httpbingo.org/forms/post')

For finding elements to interact with, use ax_tree:

root = await page.ax_tree()
print(str(root)[:300])

- **RootWebArea** "6. httpbin.org/forms/post" `focusable=True` `url=https://httpbin.org/forms/post` [#14]
  - **LabelText** "" [#20]
    - **StaticText** "Customer name: " [#62]
      - **InlineTextBox** "Customer name: "
    - **textbox** "Customer name: " `focusable=True` `editable=plaintext` `set


find and find_id are used to identify elements in the tree:

nmid = root.find_id('textbox', 'Customer name')
nmid

2


You can use regular CDP methods, or one of the provided shortcuts:

await page.fill_text(nmid, 'Jeremy Howard')
await page.click(root.find_id('radio', 'Large'))
await page.js_node_run('this.value = "18:30"', root.find_id('InputTime', 'delivery time'));

You can use click to click a button, or click_and_wait to wait for the next page to load:

await page.click_and_wait(root.find_id('button', 'Submit order'))


await page.close()


await cdp.close()

title: solvecdp
text:
Running AppleScript on your Mac
With the solvebridge menu bar app connected to your Solveit instance, osa (or async aosa) runs AppleScript on your Mac over /api/wsx?chan=mac and returns standard output:

osa('tell application "Microsoft Word" to activate')

To allow LLMs like solveit with safepyrun to access solvecdp, use:
cdp_yolo()
Then use a prompt such as:

Try using python to connect a cdp_ JsCDP object and open a page_ tab with new_page, then goto <url>, fill it out, read it to check it’s filled correctly, then submit it, and see what you get back. Don’t use find_id - you can get all the ids at once with ax_tree (don’t truncate the result of it). Don’t add extra waits etc - solvecdp handles it automatically. IDs can change so be sure to use the ax_tree IDs you read.

title: SolveitCDP API
text:
import threading
from fastcore.test import test_eq, expect_fail
Channel connects to rustygate’s /api/wsx relay for ongoing JSON messaging. Set JUPYGATE_URL to the gateway’s URL, or pass a full WebSocket url to Channel.connect. The default gateway is http://127.0.0.1:8787.
Rustygate supplies JUPYGATE_URL to every spawned kernel and trusts loopback connections; pass token= to send Authorization: Bearer <token> against a token-gated gateway. Peers join the same named channel even when the kernel connects directly over loopback and the browser or desktop app connects through Solveit’s /rusty/api/wsx proxy.
source

Channel
def Channel(
    chan, url:NoneType=None
):
Duplex JSON messaging with the other peers on a named /api/wsx relay channel
Connect each peer to the same channel name on rustygate’s /api/wsx relay. The relay forwards each frame unchanged to every other peer on that channel. solvecdp uses Channel to communicate with the solveit-chrome extension.
Channel sends JSON dictionaries. Pass the fields as keyword arguments to send. Incoming frames become AttrDict objects. If a frame’s id matches a pending request, it completes that request. Other frames go into the events queue.
Here we connect two peers and send a greeting. The second peer reads it from events.
ch1,ch2 = await Channel.connect('test'),await Channel.connect('test')
await ch1.send(hello='world')
test_eq((await ch2.events.get()).hello, 'world')
request adds a unique id and waits for a reply with that id. Requests can run concurrently. The peer answering a request must include its id in the reply. This example replies with twice the supplied number.
async def _responder():
    msg = await ch2.events.get()
    await ch2.send(id=msg.id, result=msg.x*2)

task = asyncio.create_task(_responder())
test_eq((await ch1.request(x=21)).result, 42)
Check is_open before and after closing the connections.
assert ch1.is_open
await ch1.close()
await ch2.close()
assert not ch1.is_open
source

JsCDP
def JsCDP(
    wsconn:str=None, # WebSocket URL, populated by connection helpers
    debug:bool=False, # Log protocol events
    command_timeout:float=10, # Seconds before an unanswered command raises TimeoutError
):
CDP over the solveit-chrome extension: frames relayed via rustygate’s /api/wsx channel
Everything else comes from fastcdp.ext’s ExtCDP: the sessionId↔︎tabId mapping, the lifecycle actions, and new_page/attach_page/pages. JsCDP just supplies the channel, meeting the extension at rustygate’s /api/wsx relay instead of listening on a local port (a solveit kernel usually runs in a container that the user’s browser can’t reach, so both sides dial out to the relay).
Connect, open a tab, and drive it. goto, eval, and friends are all inherited from fastcdp through the Page proxy:
cdp = await JsCDP.connect()
page = await cdp.new_page()
await page.goto('https://httpbingo.org/forms/post')
await page.eval('document.title')
assert 'httpbingo.org' in await page.eval('document.title')
assert first(await cdp.pages, lambda t: 'httpbingo' in t.get('url',''))
The accessibility tree and form helpers also come straight from fastcdp: find elements with ax_tree/find_id, then fill_text, click, select_option, and click_and_wait.
root = await page.ax_tree()
await page.fill_text(root.find_id('textbox', 'Customer name'), 'Jeremy Howard')
await page.click(root.find_id('radio', 'Large'))
await page.click(root.find_id('checkbox', 'Extra Cheese'))
await page.click_and_wait(root.find_id('button', 'Submit order'))
assert 'Jeremy Howard' in await page.eval('document.body.innerText')
The debugging buffers work too, since every chrome.debugger event is streamed over the channel and dispatched by the inherited machinery:
await page.start_console()
await page.eval(r'console.warn("watch out")')
test_eq(await page.console(r'watch'), ['warning: watch out'])
await page.close()
await cdp.close()

title: SolveitCDP API
text:
Running AppleScript with solvebridge
Because /api/wsx stores no messages and drops frames when no peer is connected, _wait_bridge waits until a solvebridge peer either replies ok: true to a ping probe or announces {"event": "hello"} on connect before sending an AppleScript command.
aosa opens a Channel (default chan='mac'), waits for solvebridge via _wait_bridge, and sends one osascript command. Replies carrying an error field (such as a user denial or unsupported platform) or a nonzero returncode raise RuntimeError.


source

aosa
async def aosa(
    script:str, # AppleScript source to run on the connected Mac
    chan:str='mac', # Relay channel name `solvebridge` connects to
    url:str=None, # Full relay URL (defaults to `/api/wsx` on `JUPYGATE_URL`)
    token:str=None, # Optional bearer token for token-gated gateways
    timeout:float=60, # Seconds to wait for approval and execution
    wait_connect:float=25, # Seconds to wait for `solvebridge` to answer `ping` or `hello`
    ping_interval:float=1.5, # Seconds between `ping` probes while waiting for `solvebridge`
)->str:
Run AppleScript script on the user’s Mac through solvebridge and return stdout


Test the full handshake and error paths against a fake bridge peer on /api/wsx: late-connecting hello wakeup, ping replies, user denials, nonzero exit codes, disconnected timeouts, and calling synchronous osa while an event loop is already running.

async def _fake_bridge(chan, delay=0, limit=None):
    if delay: await asyncio.sleep(delay)
    ch = await Channel.connect(chan)
    try:
        await ch.send(event='hello', platform='macos', app='solvebridge')
        seen = 0
        while limit is None or seen < limit:
            msg = await ch.events.get()
            if msg.get('cmd') == 'ping': await ch.send(id=msg.id, ok=True, platform='macos')
            elif msg.get('cmd') == 'osascript':
                seen += 1
                s = msg.script
                if s == 'deny': await ch.send(id=msg.id, error='denied by user')
                elif s == 'fail': await ch.send(id=msg.id, stdout='', stderr='syntax error', returncode=1)
                else: await ch.send(id=msg.id, stdout=f'ran: {s}\n', stderr='', returncode=0)
    finally: await ch.close()


bridge = asyncio.create_task(_fake_bridge('test-mac', delay=0.08, limit=3))
test_eq(await aosa('activate', chan='test-mac', ping_interval=0.05), 'ran: activate\n')
with expect_fail(RuntimeError, 'denied by user'): await aosa('deny', chan='test-mac', ping_interval=0.05)
with expect_fail(RuntimeError, 'syntax error'): await aosa('fail', chan='test-mac', ping_interval=0.05)
await bridge
with expect_fail(TimeoutError, 'not connected'): await aosa('noop', chan='test-mac-empty', wait_connect=0.15, ping_interval=0.05)

osa wraps aosa synchronously so Solveit’s py tool can run AppleScript without await, even inside a Jupyter kernel where an asyncio event loop is already running.


source

osa
def osa(
    script:str, # AppleScript source to run on the connected Mac
    *, chan:str='mac', # Relay channel name `solvebridge` connects to
    url:str=None, # Full relay URL (defaults to `/api/wsx` on `JUPYGATE_URL`)
    token:str=None, # Optional bearer token for token-gated gateways
    timeout:float=60, # Seconds to wait for approval and execution
    wait_connect:float=25, # Seconds to wait for `solvebridge` to answer `ping` or `hello`
    ping_interval:float=1.5, # Seconds between `ping` probes while waiting for `solvebridge`
)->str:
Run AppleScript script synchronously on the user’s Mac through solvebridge and return stdout



t = threading.Thread(target=asyncio.run, args=(_fake_bridge('test-mac-sync', delay=0.05, limit=1),))
t.start()
test_eq(osa('tell Word', chan='test-mac-sync', ping_interval=0.05), 'ran: tell Word\n')
t.join(2)
assert not t.is_alive()
